tradition.name: British math rock
tradition.lineage: A British math-rock network including TTNG, Delta Sleep, Orchards and Three Trapped Tigers. The selected TTNG trio branch combines clean two-handed guitar figures, an independent low six-string part, drums with shifting accents, and melodic lead singing.

extras.description: This is a song-facing math-rock model, not an automatically instrumental national style. The arrangement lets intricate tapped guitar and bass-baritone lines remain distinct beneath a sung melody. Uneven groupings and changes of accent provide motion without requiring one fixed unusual time signature. It differs from the selected British post-rock model by favoring compact, articulated counterpoint over sustained guitar/synth washes.

entries.geo_rationale: TTNG’s first-person formation account and label-hosted interview establish Oxford as this branch’s origin. The cited 2016 recording was made in Chicago, not Oxford.

tradition.lineage: Indie folk argentino is a discovery network including Mía Maestro and other Argentine-connected performers. Maestro’s Si Agua combines bilingual songwriting with acoustic, keyboard and arranged string parts in an international recording context.

entries.geo_rationale: Representative documented practice anchor for the selected branch; not an exclusive birthplace or the limit of this wider discovery category.

tradition.name: Midwest Americana
tradition.lineage: Midwest Americana connects roots song and performance communities across the American Midwest. Charlie Parr’s Minnesota-based blues and folk songwriting supplies one documented twelve-string-guitar branch, without making it the region’s only sound.

extras.description: A lead singing voice sits above fingerpicked twelve-string guitar, with paired-string resonance and spare production. Parr’s label documents both standard and open-C setups; standard pairs are selected here, while guitar body, microphones and room are authored choices.

entries.geo_rationale: Representative documented practice anchor for the selected branch; not an exclusive birthplace or the limit of this wider discovery category.

tradition.name: Bhojpuri folk
tradition.lineage: Bhojpuri-language folk practice in eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar includes migration songs, birha, seasonal and life-cycle repertories. Field biographies and documented ensembles establish voice, harmonium, dholak and small cymbals for the selected contemporary sung branch.

extras.description: A lead singer exchanges short phrases with supporting voices over harmonium chords, dholak patterns and manjira timekeeping. The selected recording model reflects documented ensemble roles without treating every Bhojpuri song as a wedding or devotional performance; tuning, drum wood and string-free studio setup are authored defaults.

entries.geo_rationale: Representative documented practice anchor for the selected branch; not an exclusive birthplace or the limit of this wider discovery category.

tradition.name: Folk siciliana
tradition.lineage: Sicilian folk encompasses sung narratives and diverse local instrumental practices. Alfio Antico’s documented dialect singing, shepherd-memory narratives and hand-built frame drums provide the selected drum-and-voice branch.

extras.description: Voice and a hand-played jingled frame drum alternate pulse, flourishes and text-led pauses. Antico describes making drum frames, membranes and metal jingles himself; the recipe preserves that instrument family while treating exact wood, skin and studio settings as authored choices, not documented specifications of his instruments.

entries.geo_rationale: Representative documented practice anchor for the selected branch; not an exclusive birthplace or the limit of this wider discovery category. Full researched anchor: Catania, Sicily.

tradition.name: Greek folk

extras.description: A strongly inflected voice alternates with bowed lyra melody and plucked laouto support. The arrangement preserves the distinct Cretan bowed fiddle and long-neck lute, while bowing detail, room, materials and digital recording chain are authored defaults rather than a transcription of a historical wedding.

entries.geo_rationale: Representative documented practice anchor for the selected branch; not an exclusive birthplace or the limit of this wider discovery category.

data_checks.scope: Only private copies of01/02 data changed; actual original _loader/_merge and validate.js are used. No engine/build/UI/compiler edits or exact-render-equality requirement.

house-rock-dependencies.rationale: Merged electric_technique has clean arpeggiation but no fretboard-tapping technique; TTNG label-hosted Audiotree account and drummer interview explicitly document the distinct two-hand approach. Reusable technique variant, not an instrument or compulsory default for existing genres.

The three current bass_vi_technique choices are tic-tac, surf lead and doom chords. The source describes an independently composed six-string bass-baritone part fitting around TTNG guitar and drums; a neutral melodic/chordal choice avoids falsely prescribing those unrelated idioms.

variant.name: Melodic lead in amplified rock ensemble

house-rock-dependencies.rationale: Existing suona_context choices impose procession, opera/bangzi or solo-showpiece technique. Cui Jian’s documented integration of suona with electric rock calls for a neutral rock-ensemble context without a new instrument or unsupported flutter-tonguing.

variants.name: Five strings CGDAE, added low C

house-rock-dependencies.rationale: The existing fiddle has no string-count/range selection. Holas directly describes adding a viola C string and later commissioning a purpose-built five-string violin. A source-unspecified empty-descriptor default preserves existing recipes; the optional extension does not turn every fiddle into this instrument.
Existing Rhodes uses force jazz-chordal or soul/R&B context. Switchfoot’s documented processed Rhodes supports a neutral band-song role.
Existing contexts force1990s production, township dance or wedding accompaniment. A modern band layer is directly documented.
The source names Korg M3. Existing M1, JV, home-keyboard and arranger variants cannot accurately represent it. Korg’s operation guide documents EDS multisample/velocity-layer architecture.
An authored sample-workstation realization should not silently claim a Korg M1, Roland JV or arranger model when credits name only keyboards. Nonautomatic neutral option preserves existing defaults.

Existing overdriven lead does not express pitch bending, and slide/bottleneck is a different physical technique. Bonamassa’s firsthand account explicitly places controlled bends and in-between pitch inflections at the center of his lead phrasing. This optional reusable technique does not retune the whole band.

The source explicitly credits a five-string Yamaha bass. Existing electric_bass parts include pickup, string material and scale but no string count. Empty source-unspecified default preserves all existing recipes; optional five-string selection records a real construction distinction.

Olympic credits Kronos, while the current named variants predate it or specify arranger keyboards. This selects its documented HD-1 sample-playback component, not all nine synthesis engines or the separate Nord C1.
Existing P-only, J/J, MM humbucker and active soapbar configurations do not represent the credited Yamaha BB2025X split-coil plus blade-style bridge pickup combination.

Existing feedback-drone, tremolo-picking and sustained-loop choices do not describe a handheld driver physically sustaining the string without repeated picking. Direct Lasek testimony documents EBow lines; the manufacturer explains magnetic string excitation. This is a technique variant, not a new guitar.

variant.name: Electric-piano layer in an amplified rock band

house-rock-dependencies.rationale: The existing contexts are named Ray Charles and Supertramp. A neutral optional band-layer context represents the documented HIM keyboard use without attaching an unsupported artist-specific identity.

The only current technique is chopped samples. A fixed-voice PCM rhythm machine uses programmed drum one-shots, not necessarily chopped breaks. Band/engineer accounts establish drum-machine practice and Yamaha describes the RX series PCM architecture.
Existing pitched-kick, chopped-break and dense-layered options all assert processing not necessary for this documented rhythm-programmer branch. This optional setting retains the discrete PCM voices.

The inspected manufacturer history confirms PCM but not a numeric word length. A neutral nonautomatic option avoids asserting either modern high-resolution or a specific historical bit depth without primary evidence.

The semi-hollow category currently offers only explicitly clean strumming/arpeggios or jazz comping. A nonautomatic overdriven strum is needed for the source-supported amplified punk/rockabilly branch without labeling it clean jazz.

Manufacturer associates the band with Verythin guitars; its CT specification documents spruce center block and628mm scale. The optional CT configuration is an explicitly authored member of that family, not a claim to identify a musician’s exact specimen.

Current vibraphone parts cover motor and mallets but omit its sounding-bar material. Manufacturer documentation supports an aluminum-alloy option; a descriptor-free unspecified baseline preserves existing records. The chosen alloy is an authored implementation, not an inferred Hurtmold make/model.

variant.name: Two-string electric bass, low E–A pair

house-rock-dependencies.rationale: Stig Pedersen and Jacob Binzer directly describe the two-string bass construction and E/A selection. This is a string-count/tuning configuration on the existing electric bass, not a new instrument invented for a body shape. It shares the descriptor-free baseline part introduced in packet021.

variant.name: Pitch organization not specified by source

bass-metal-dependent.rationale: The documented harsh, barked and growled metal voices do not establish equal-tempered fixed pitches, a modal system, or continuous microtonal glides. Current fixed-pitch default therefore adds an unsupported audible claim even when quality and register are source-unspecified. This explicitly selected empty variant records absence of evidence without declaring all harsh vocals unpitched and without changing existing defaults or anatomy. The already-existing voice_microtone_local_unspecified is selected alongside it.

variant.name: Korg Triton Extreme (2004 PCM workstation / sampler)

bass-metal-dependent.rationale: Vadim Pruzhanov explicitly identifies the Triton Extreme for the documented DragonForce-era composition/sampling practice. Korg's own history and technical documentation identify the 2004 PCM/sampling workstation. This is a hardware lineage on the existing ROM workstation instrument, not a new keyboard instrument or a falsely labeled analog synthesizer.

The existing context choices impose 90s sequenced pop, township MIDI or one-person wedding accompaniment. The documented ensemble keyboard role does not establish any of those. This empty sonic context avoids invented sequencing/cultural claims while the actual playing and preset controls remain explicit.

Bill Steer directly identifies Carcass's B tuning and five-semitone lowering. This is a six-string tuning distinct from drop B; it does not justify a new baritone instrument or a seven-string substitute.

Modern Drummer's direct Derek Roddy interview describes the pattern and distinguishes single-foot from double-bass approaches. The existing double-kick part is retained as an independent equipment dimension: a double pedal alone is not a blast beat, and a blast does not universally require two feet.

Official opera-company voice classifications establish the distinction. Tessitura is independent of phonation register: chest voice alone does not encode a bass singer, while fry, strohbass and oktavist impose unsupported techniques. No numeric pitch limits or sex inference is encoded. The empty source-unspecified default preserves old sonic output; the two informative variants are explicit-only. These are capabilities on the existing voice instrument, not new instruments or an expanded all-Fach classification scheme.
